name: Mailbutler
tagline: Email tracking, scheduling, notes, contacts, and AI assistance

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: No published numeric email cap; 14-day all-feature trial falls back to Starter; every sent email carries a visible Mailbutler watermark.
tiers.notes: Free forever; basic tracking/notifications and signature marketing only; Smart Assistant excluded.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: No published numeric send cap; includes templates, mail merge, assignments, notes/tasks/tags and automations; Smart Assistant excluded.

tiers.name: Smart
tiers.limits: No published numeric send or AI quota; adds per-recipient tracking plus Smart Compose, Improve, Timing, Follow-ups, Task Finder and Summarize.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Custom plan; no numeric caps published; adds a custom subdomain, CRM tracking sync and advanced signature controls.
tiers.notes: Custom quote; custom SMTP is marked coming soon.

pricing.freeTierCaps: No published numeric email cap; $0 forever, but every sent email includes a visible Mailbutler watermark; 14-day full-feature trial
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (up to 25% off); USD/EUR; 14-day trial, no card
pricing.hiddenCosts: Mail Merge is constrained by the connected email provider's sending limits; Smart Assistant requires Smart or Business after trial; Business has no public price and custom SMTP is still marked coming soon.

verdictSummary: The visible email productivity add-on loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Mailbutler earns its keep through deliverability, security, integration, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local email companion for email productivity add-on that works on exported mail or one user-authorized IMAP account.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: IMAP or Gmail OAuth credentials where supported
whatYouLose: team routing and shared inbox rules
calendar-provider edge cases and timezone correctness
whyPeopleStillPay: Mailbutler: Email is infrastructure. Customers pay to avoid lost messages, broken auth, spam problems, and the reputational cost of a flaky inbox.
ongoingBurden: Own OAuth refresh, IMAP quirks, encryption, spam handling, notification delivery, and provider policy changes.

priorArt.name: Mailspring
priorArt.desc: Open-source desktop mail client and useful IMAP prior art.

rejectedAlternatives.name: BlueMail Personal
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Capped AI drafting is not tracking, scheduling, notes and contact management.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mailspring
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Tracking and scheduling are Pro, while notes and contact enrichment are not a replacement.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Spark Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Scheduling is free, but read status and AI are paid and contact notes never become a CRM.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Mailbutler is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Mailbutler, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local email companion for email productivity add-on that works on exported mail or one user-authorized IMAP account.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: team routing and shared inbox rules; abuse response and security operations; calendar-provider edge cases and timezone correctness.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
